question: Strength-1 Crisis against Company-controlled region; only available defense is one active unused local alliance with printed strength 2.
exhausted_piece: the sole strength-2 local alliance, moved entirely to bottom half of its Army box
authority_classification: Reasoned application of explicit published rules, worked example, and player aid; not a verbatim scenario ruling or external FAQ.

literal_statements: P22 defines alliances as temporary Army pieces whose strength can be used for Deploy or defense. Each piece is usable only once on the purchase turn; its strength cannot be split among purposes.
P22 makes printed alliance dice the contribution to Deploy and defines exhaustion by moving the whole piece to the bottom half of its Army box.
P33 requires exhaustion equal to Crisis strength or as many as possible, and uses the words newly-exhausted pieces do not equal for failure.
P29 expressly gives 2 officers + 2 regiments + Jagat Seths collective strength 6.
Player aid p2 gives a shared defender-wins-ties comparison and includes exhausted alliances in Company defender strength.
reasoned_application: For strength comparison, pieces cannot consistently mean an unweighted count of physical objects: p29 has five physical combat pieces but strength six. Officers/regiments contribute one apiece and the alliance contributes its printed two. Pieces still means actual whole objects for exhaustion.

The aid comparison is a threshold comparison: attacker succeeds when stronger; matching or exceeding the attack defends. P33 equal is read as meeting the required defense, not an exact-total ceiling that makes a stronger indivisible alliance lose.

The sole available alliance must be used under the mandatory defense obligation. Move the one whole piece, apply its two strength to this one defense, stop the strength-one attack. There is no defense success roll.

Unused capacity is wasted for this use; no strength pip, residual marker, second use, or later defense is retained. Once-only use independently bars using one alliance in two separate defenses, even if both are called defense as a general purpose.

alternative_readings.reading: One physical object always counts one defense regardless of alliance printing.
alternative_readings.basis: Contradicts p22 making alliance strength usable for defense and the p29 five-objects/strength-six worked example. It happens to defend strength 1 but fails strength 2 incorrectly.

alternative_readings.reading: Add printed strength, but require exact numerical equality; full strength 2 therefore loses to attack 1.
alternative_readings.basis: Treats p33 equal as an exact ceiling despite the player aid shared defender comparison and the p22 whole-piece strength rule. The aid table supports superior defense, with ties also defended.

alternative_readings.reading: Spend one strength from the alliance now and save one for later.
alternative_readings.basis: P22 uses whole-piece exhaustion and once-only use; it expressly bars splitting among purposes. There is no partial-exhaustion or strength-bank mechanism in the inspected rules.

alternative_readings.reading: Commit the whole indivisible strength-2 alliance and meet the attack requirement, with surplus unavailable later.
alternative_readings.basis: Reconciles p22, p29, p33 and the player aid without treating alliance printing as irrelevant or creating partial pieces.

strength_2_crisis_same_army.basis: The same whole alliance supplies two defense strength; exact tie is sufficient.

strength_3_or_more_same_army.basis: Exhaust all available pieces; two defense strength is insufficient, so Crisis succeeds and Region Loss follows.

one_indivisible_alliance_exceeds_require.basis: Reasoned threshold application of the sources, supported by player aid; excess is consumed with the whole piece.

generalizations.arbitrary_excess_exhaustion_when_other_s: Not decided here. The sources require meeting strength or exhausting as many as possible, and do not explicitly provide an optimization rule for every possible mixture of differently valued pieces.

remaining_uncertainty.precise_editorial_issue: P33 alone does not explicitly write weighted sum or at least and uses equal. The p22 strength rule, p29 worked example, and aid comparison resolve this case when read together. No scenario-specific sentence explicitly narrates strength 2 versus strength 1.
remaining_uncertainty.unresolved_adjacent_issue: The inspected passages do not state a general minimum-excess selection algorithm for multiple differently valued eligible pieces; no such algorithm is needed with only one piece.
